newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-COX PUSHES TASMANIA CLOSER TO FINAL BERTH.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-COX PUSHES TASMANIA CLOSER TO FINAL BERTH.

text.p: Tasmania opener Jamie Cox scored a century against New South Wales on Thursday to lift his side closer to a place in the Sheffield Shield final.
Cox dominated weak bowling to hit 143 in Tasmania's commanding first innings total of 370 for four on the first day in Sydney.
Tasmania will meet Shield leaders Western Australia in next week's final in Perth if they can build on their strong batting performance to record an outright victory, regardless of results elswhere.
Middle order batsman Ricky Ponting, who is fighting for a place on Australia's forthcoming tour to England, furthered his claim with a sparkling 64.
New South Wales, who must beat Tasmania to have any chance of playing in the final, were handicapped by the absence of fast bowler Glenn McGrath, on test duty in South Africa.
Fellow fast bowlers Anthony Stuart and Phil Alley were also unavailable for the home side because of injury.
Queensland, who must beat South Australia in Brisbane and then hope for a favourable result in Sydney, hit back late in the day to reduce the visitors to 26 for three after being dismissed for 277.
